verses.text: Salamanasar king of the Assyrians went up against him. Hoshea became his slave and paid him manaa.
verses.display_text: Salamanasar king of the Assyrians went up against him. Hoshea became his slave and paid him manaa.

verses.text: The king of the Assyrians found wrongdoing in Hoshea, because he had sent messengers to Segor king of Egypt and had not brought manaa to the king of the Assyrians in that year. The king of the Assyrians besieged him and bound him in prison.
verses.display_text: The king of the Assyrians found wrongdoing in Hoshea, because he had sent messengers to Segor king of Egypt and had not brought manaa to the king of the Assyrians in that year. The king of the Assyrians besieged him and bound him in prison.

verses.text: The king of the Assyrians went up through the whole land, went up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.
verses.display_text: The king of the Assyrians went up through the whole land, went up to Samaria, and besieged it for three years.

verses.text: In Hoshea’s ninth year the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria and deported Israel to the Assyrians. He settled them in Alae and Abor, rivers of Gozan, and Ore of the Medes.
verses.display_text: In Hoshea’s ninth year the king of the Assyrians captured Samaria and deported Israel to the Assyrians. He settled them in Alae and Abor, rivers of Gozan, and Ore of the Medes.

verses.text: This happened because the Israelites sinned against the Lord their God, who brought them up from Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.
verses.display_text: This happened because the Israelites sinned against the Lord their God, who brought them up from Egypt, from under the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and they feared other gods.

verses.text: They walked in the ordinances of the nations whom the Lord removed before the Israelites; and Israel’s kings, all who acted so,
verses.display_text: They walked in the ordinances of the nations whom the Lord removed before the Israelites; and Israel’s kings, all who acted so,

verses.text: and all the Israelites who clothed themselves in words that were not so against the Lord their God, built themselves high places in all their cities, from watchtower to fortified city.
verses.display_text: and all the Israelites who clothed themselves in words that were not so against the Lord their God, built themselves high places in all their cities, from watchtower to fortified city.

verses.text: They set up pillars and groves for themselves on every high hill and under every leafy tree.
verses.display_text: They set up pillars and groves for themselves on every high hill and under every leafy tree.

verses.text: They burned incense there at all the high places like the nations whom the Lord deported before them. They made associates and engraved, to provoke the Lord.
verses.display_text: They burned incense there at all the high places like the nations whom the Lord deported before them. They made associates and engraved, to provoke the Lord.

verses.text: They served the idols, concerning which the Lord had said to them, ‘You shall not do this thing to the Lord.’
verses.display_text: They served the idols, concerning which the Lord had said to them, ‘You shall not do this thing to the Lord.’

verses.text: The Lord warned Israel and Judah through all His prophets, every seer: ‘Turn from your evil ways and keep My commandments, My ordinances, and all the law I commanded your fathers, all that I sent to them through My servants the prophets.’
verses.display_text: The Lord warned Israel and Judah through all His prophets, every seer: ‘Turn from your evil ways and keep My commandments, My ordinances, and all the law I commanded your fathers, all that I sent to them through My servants the prophets.’

verses.text: But they did not listen. They hardened their back more than the back of their fathers.
verses.display_text: But they did not listen. They hardened their back more than the back of their fathers.

verses.text: They did not keep His testimonies by which He warned them. They followed vain things and became vain, and followed the nations around them, concerning whom He had commanded them not to do such things.
verses.display_text: They did not keep His testimonies by which He warned them. They followed vain things and became vain, and followed the nations around them, concerning whom He had commanded them not to do such things.

verses.text: They abandoned the commandments of the Lord their God. They made a casting for themselves, two heifers, made groves, bowed down to all heaven’s host, and served Baal.
verses.display_text: They abandoned the commandments of the Lord their God. They made a casting for themselves, two heifers, made groves, bowed down to all heaven’s host, and served Baal.

verses.text: They led their sons and daughters through fire, practiced divinations, read omens, and were sold to do evil in the Lord’s eyes, provoking Him.
verses.display_text: They led their sons and daughters through fire, practiced divinations, read omens, and were sold to do evil in the Lord’s eyes, provoking Him.

verses.text: The Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them from His presence. None remained except the tribe of Judah alone.
verses.display_text: The Lord was very angry with Israel and removed them from His presence. None remained except the tribe of Judah alone.

verses.text: Judah also did not keep the commandments of the Lord their God; they walked in the ordinances Israel had made.
verses.display_text: Judah also did not keep the commandments of the Lord their God; they walked in the ordinances Israel had made.

verses.text: They rejected the Lord throughout all Israel’s seed; He shook them and gave them into the hands of those plundering them, until He cast them from His presence.
verses.display_text: They rejected the Lord throughout all Israel’s seed; He shook them and gave them into the hands of those plundering them, until He cast them from His presence.

verses.text: For Israel was apart from David’s house, and they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king. Jeroboam thrust Israel away from following the Lord and caused them to commit a great sin.
verses.display_text: For Israel was apart from David’s house, and they made Jeroboam son of Nebat king. Jeroboam thrust Israel away from following the Lord and caused them to commit a great sin.

verses.text: The Israelites walked in every sin Jeroboam committed; they did not turn away from it,
verses.display_text: The Israelites walked in every sin Jeroboam committed; they did not turn away from it,

verses.text: until the Lord removed Israel from His presence, as the Lord had spoken through all His servants the prophets. Israel was deported from its land to the Assyrians, to this day.
verses.display_text: until the Lord removed Israel from His presence, as the Lord had spoken through all His servants the prophets. Israel was deported from its land to the Assyrians, to this day.

verses.text: The king of the Assyrians brought from Babylon the one from Chountha, and from Aia, Aimath, and Seppharouain. They were settled in Samaria’s cities in place of the Israelites, took possession of Samaria, and lived in its cities.
verses.display_text: The king of the Assyrians brought from Babylon the one from Chountha, and from Aia, Aimath, and Seppharouain. They were settled in Samaria’s cities in place of the Israelites, took possession of Samaria, and lived in its cities.

verses.text: At the beginning of their residence, they did not fear the Lord. The Lord sent lions among them, and they killed some of them.
verses.display_text: At the beginning of their residence, they did not fear the Lord. The Lord sent lions among them, and they killed some of them.

verses.text: They told the king of the Assyrians, ‘The nations you did deport and did resettle in Samaria’s cities do not know the judgment of the God of the land. He has sent lions among them, and behold, they are killing them, because they do not know the judgment of the God of the land.’
verses.display_text: They told the king of the Assyrians, ‘The nations you did deport and did resettle in Samaria’s cities do not know the judgment of the God of the land. He has sent lions among them, and behold, they are killing them, because they do not know the judgment of the God of the land.’

verses.text: The king of the Assyrians commanded, ‘Take away from there; let them go and live there, and they shall enlighten them about the judgment of the God of the land.’
verses.display_text: The king of the Assyrians commanded, ‘Take away from there; let them go and live there, and they shall enlighten them about the judgment of the God of the land.’

verses.text: They brought one of the priests whom they had deported from Samaria, and he lived in Bethel. He enlightened them about how to fear the Lord.
verses.display_text: They brought one of the priests whom they had deported from Samaria, and he lived in Bethel. He enlightened them about how to fear the Lord.

verses.text: But each nation made its own gods and placed them in the house of the high places which the Samaritans had made, the nations in their cities where they lived.
verses.display_text: But each nation made its own gods and placed them in the house of the high places which the Samaritans had made, the nations in their cities where they lived.

verses.text: The men of Babylon made Sokchothbainith; the men of Chouth made Nerigel; the men of Aimath made Asimath.
verses.display_text: The men of Babylon made Sokchothbainith; the men of Chouth made Nerigel; the men of Aimath made Asimath.

verses.text: The Evites made Eblazer and Tharthak, and the Seppharouain burned their sons in fire to Adramelech and Anemelech, gods of Seppharouain.
verses.display_text: The Evites made Eblazer and Tharthak, and the Seppharouain burned their sons in fire to Adramelech and Anemelech, gods of Seppharouain.

verses.text: They feared the Lord and installed their abominations in the houses of the high places they had made in Samaria, each nation in the city where it lived. They feared the Lord and made priests of the high places for themselves, and performed rites for themselves in the house of the high places.
verses.display_text: They feared the Lord and installed their abominations in the houses of the high places they had made in Samaria, each nation in the city where it lived. They feared the Lord and made priests of the high places for themselves, and performed rites for themselves in the house of the high places.

verses.text: They feared the Lord while serving their own gods, according to the judgment of the nations from which he had deported them.
verses.display_text: They feared the Lord while serving their own gods, according to the judgment of the nations from which he had deported them.

verses.text: To this day they acted according to their judgment. They fear, and they act according to their ordinances, their judgment, the law, and the commandment which the Lord commanded Jacob’s sons, whom He named Israel.
verses.display_text: To this day they acted according to their judgment. They fear, and they act according to their ordinances, their judgment, the law, and the commandment which the Lord commanded Jacob’s sons, whom He named Israel.

verses.text: The Lord made a covenant with them and commanded them, ‘You shall not fear other gods, bow down to them, serve them, or sacrifice to them,
verses.display_text: The Lord made a covenant with them and commanded them, ‘You shall not fear other gods, bow down to them, serve them, or sacrifice to them,

verses.text: but only the Lord, who brought you up from Egypt with great strength and a raised arm—Him you shall fear, to Him you shall bow down, and to Him you shall sacrifice.
verses.display_text: but only the Lord, who brought you up from Egypt with great strength and a raised arm—Him you shall fear, to Him you shall bow down, and to Him you shall sacrifice.

verses.text: The ordinances, judgments, law, and commandments He wrote for you, you shall take care to perform all the days; you shall not fear other gods.
verses.display_text: The ordinances, judgments, law, and commandments He wrote for you, you shall take care to perform all the days; you shall not fear other gods.

verses.text: You shall not forget the covenant He made with you, and you shall not fear other gods.
verses.display_text: You shall not forget the covenant He made with you, and you shall not fear other gods.

verses.text: But you shall fear the Lord your God, and He will rescue you from all your enemies.
verses.display_text: But you shall fear the Lord your God, and He will rescue you from all your enemies.

verses.text: You shall not listen to their judgment, which they themselves practice.’
verses.display_text: You shall not listen to their judgment, which they themselves practice.’

verses.text: These nations feared the Lord while serving their carved images. Their sons and their sons’ sons also do as their fathers did, to this day.
verses.display_text: These nations feared the Lord while serving their carved images. Their sons and their sons’ sons also do as their fathers did, to this day.

verses.text: In the third year of Hoshea son of Ela, king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz, king of Judah, became king.
verses.display_text: In the third year of Hoshea son of Ela, king of Israel, Hezekiah son of Ahaz, king of Judah, became king.

verses.text: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Abou daughter of Zechariah.
verses.display_text: He was twenty-five years old when he became king, and he reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Abou daughter of Zechariah.

verses.text: He did what was right in the Lord’s eyes, in accordance with everything his father David had done.
verses.display_text: He did what was right in the Lord’s eyes, in accordance with everything his father David had done.

verses.text: He removed the high places, shattered all the pillars, and destroyed the groves and the bronze serpent Moses had made, because until those days the Israelites burned incense to it. He called it Neesthan.
verses.display_text: He removed the high places, shattered all the pillars, and destroyed the groves and the bronze serpent Moses had made, because until those days the Israelites burned incense to it. He called it Neesthan.

verses.text: He hoped in the Lord, Israel’s God. Among Judah’s kings there was none like him after him, nor among those before him.
verses.display_text: He hoped in the Lord, Israel’s God. Among Judah’s kings there was none like him after him, nor among those before him.

verses.text: He clung to the Lord, did not turn away from following Him, and kept His commandments which He commanded Moses.
verses.display_text: He clung to the Lord, did not turn away from following Him, and kept His commandments which He commanded Moses.

verses.text: The Lord was with him; in everything he did, he acted with understanding. He broke with the king of the Assyrians and did not serve him.
verses.display_text: The Lord was with him; in everything he did, he acted with understanding. He broke with the king of the Assyrians and did not serve him.

verses.text: He struck the foreigners as far as Gaza and its boundary, from watchtower to fortified city.
verses.display_text: He struck the foreigners as far as Gaza and its boundary, from watchtower to fortified city.

verses.text: In King Hezekiah’s fourth year—which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Ela, king of Israel—Salamanassar king of the Assyrians went up against Samaria and besieged it.
verses.display_text: In King Hezekiah’s fourth year—which was the seventh year of Hoshea son of Ela, king of Israel—Salamanassar king of the Assyrians went up against Samaria and besieged it.

verses.text: He captured it at the end of three years, in Hezekiah’s sixth year—which was Hoshea king of Israel’s ninth year—and Samaria was captured.
verses.display_text: He captured it at the end of three years, in Hezekiah’s sixth year—which was Hoshea king of Israel’s ninth year—and Samaria was captured.

verses.text: The king of the Assyrians deported Samaria to the Assyrians and placed them in Alae, on the Abor, the river of Gozan, and in Ore of the Medes.
verses.display_text: The king of the Assyrians deported Samaria to the Assyrians and placed them in Alae, on the Abor, the river of Gozan, and in Ore of the Medes.

verses.text: This was because they did not listen to the voice of the Lord their God but transgressed His covenant, everything Moses the Lord’s servant commanded. They neither listened nor acted.
verses.display_text: This was because they did not listen to the voice of the Lord their God but transgressed His covenant, everything Moses the Lord’s servant commanded. They neither listened nor acted.

verses.text: In King Hezekiah’s fourteenth year, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians went up against Judah’s fortified cities and captured them.
verses.display_text: In King Hezekiah’s fourteenth year, Sennacherib king of the Assyrians went up against Judah’s fortified cities and captured them.

verses.text: Hezekiah king of Judah sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians at Lachish: ‘I have sinned. Withdraw from me; whatever you impose on me, I will bear.’ The king of the Assyrians imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.
verses.display_text: Hezekiah king of Judah sent messengers to the king of the Assyrians at Lachish: ‘I have sinned. Withdraw from me; whatever you impose on me, I will bear.’ The king of the Assyrians imposed on Hezekiah king of Judah three hundred talents of silver and thirty talents of gold.

verses.text: Hezekiah gave all the silver found in the Lord’s house and in the treasuries of the king’s house.
verses.display_text: Hezekiah gave all the silver found in the Lord’s house and in the treasuries of the king’s house.

verses.text: At that time Hezekiah cut apart the doors of the Lord’s sanctuary and the fixed supports which Hezekiah king of Judah had gilded, and gave them to the king of the Assyrians.
verses.display_text: At that time Hezekiah cut apart the doors of the Lord’s sanctuary and the fixed supports which Hezekiah king of Judah had gilded, and gave them to the king of the Assyrians.

verses.text: The king of the Assyrians sent Tharthan, Raphis, and Rhapsakes from Lachish to King Hezekiah against Jerusalem with a great force. They went up, came to Jerusalem, and stood at the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road of the Fuller’s Field.
verses.display_text: The king of the Assyrians sent Tharthan, Raphis, and Rhapsakes from Lachish to King Hezekiah against Jerusalem with a great force. They went up, came to Jerusalem, and stood at the aqueduct of the upper pool, on the road of the Fuller’s Field.

verses.text: They called to Hezekiah. Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward, Somnas the scribe, and Joash son of Asaph the recorder went out to him.
verses.display_text: They called to Hezekiah. Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward, Somnas the scribe, and Joash son of Asaph the recorder went out to him.

verses.text: Rhapsakes said to them, ‘Tell Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians: What is this confidence in which you trust?
verses.display_text: Rhapsakes said to them, ‘Tell Hezekiah: Thus says the great king, the king of the Assyrians: What is this confidence in which you trust?

verses.text: You said—only words of lips!—“Counsel and strength for war.” Now then, in whom do you trust, that you have broken with me?
verses.display_text: You said—only words of lips!—“Counsel and strength for war.” Now then, in whom do you trust, that you have broken with me?

verses.text: Now behold, you have put your trust in this broken reed staff, Egypt. If a man supports himself on it, it enters his hand and pierces it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust him.
verses.display_text: Now behold, you have put your trust in this broken reed staff, Egypt. If a man supports himself on it, it enters his hand and pierces it. So is Pharaoh king of Egypt to all who trust him.

verses.text: Since you said to me, “We trust the Lord God,” is He not the One whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, “Before this altar you shall bow down in Jerusalem”?
verses.display_text: Since you said to me, “We trust the Lord God,” is He not the One whose high places and altars Hezekiah removed, saying to Judah and Jerusalem, “Before this altar you shall bow down in Jerusalem”?

verses.text: Now join yourselves to my master, the king of the Assyrians. I will give you two thousand horses if you can provide riders for them.
verses.display_text: Now join yourselves to my master, the king of the Assyrians. I will give you two thousand horses if you can provide riders for them.

verses.text: How can you turn back the face of one district governor, one of my master’s least servants? Yet you hope in Egypt for chariots and horsemen!
verses.display_text: How can you turn back the face of one district governor, one of my master’s least servants? Yet you hope in Egypt for chariots and horsemen!

verses.text: Now have we come up without the Lord against this place to destroy it? The Lord said to me, “Go up against this land and destroy it.”’
verses.display_text: Now have we come up without the Lord against this place to destroy it? The Lord said to me, “Go up against this land and destroy it.”’

verses.text: Eliakim son of Chelkias, Somnas, and Joash said to Rhapsakes, ‘Please speak to your servants in Syrian, for we understand it. Do not speak with us in Judean. Why are you speaking within the hearing of the people on the wall?’
verses.display_text: Eliakim son of Chelkias, Somnas, and Joash said to Rhapsakes, ‘Please speak to your servants in Syrian, for we understand it. Do not speak with us in Judean. Why are you speaking within the hearing of the people on the wall?’

verses.text: Rhapsakes said to them, ‘Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you? Was it not to the men sitting on the wall, who are to eat their own dung and drink their own urine together with you?’
verses.display_text: Rhapsakes said to them, ‘Has my master sent me to speak these words to your master and to you? Was it not to the men sitting on the wall, who are to eat their own dung and drink their own urine together with you?’

verses.text: Rhapsakes stood and cried out loudly in Judean: ‘Hear the words of the great king of the Assyrians!
verses.display_text: Rhapsakes stood and cried out loudly in Judean: ‘Hear the words of the great king of the Assyrians!

verses.text: Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah lift you up with words, for he cannot rescue you from my hand.
verses.display_text: Thus says the king: Do not let Hezekiah lift you up with words, for he cannot rescue you from my hand.

verses.text: Do not let Hezekiah make you hope in the Lord by saying, “The Lord will surely rescue us; this city will certainly not be handed into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.”
verses.display_text: Do not let Hezekiah make you hope in the Lord by saying, “The Lord will surely rescue us; this city will certainly not be handed into the hand of the king of the Assyrians.”

verses.text: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of the Assyrians: Make a blessing with me and come out to me. Each man shall drink from his vine, eat from his fig tree, and drink water from his cistern,
verses.display_text: Do not listen to Hezekiah, for thus says the king of the Assyrians: Make a blessing with me and come out to me. Each man shall drink from his vine, eat from his fig tree, and drink water from his cistern,

verses.text: until I come and take you to a land like your own, a land of grain, wine, bread, and vineyards, a land of oil-bearing olives and honey. You will live and certainly not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah, because he deceives you, saying, “The Lord will rescue us.”
verses.display_text: until I come and take you to a land like your own, a land of grain, wine, bread, and vineyards, a land of oil-bearing olives and honey. You will live and certainly not die. Do not listen to Hezekiah, because he deceives you, saying, “The Lord will rescue us.”

verses.text: Have the gods of the nations ever rescued, each his own country, from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?
verses.display_text: Have the gods of the nations ever rescued, each his own country, from the hand of the king of the Assyrians?

verses.text: Where is the god of Aimath and Arphad? Where is the god of Seppharouain? And have they rescued Samaria from my hand?
verses.display_text: Where is the god of Aimath and Arphad? Where is the god of Seppharouain? And have they rescued Samaria from my hand?

verses.text: Who among all the gods of the lands has rescued their lands from my hand, that the Lord should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?’
verses.display_text: Who among all the gods of the lands has rescued their lands from my hand, that the Lord should rescue Jerusalem from my hand?’

verses.text: They kept silent and did not answer him a word, for the king had commanded, ‘Do not answer him.’
verses.display_text: They kept silent and did not answer him a word, for the king had commanded, ‘Do not answer him.’

verses.text: Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward, Somnas the scribe, and Joash son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with torn garments and reported Rhapsakes’s words to him.
verses.display_text: Eliakim son of Chelkias the steward, Somnas the scribe, and Joash son of Asaph the recorder came to Hezekiah with torn garments and reported Rhapsakes’s words to him.

verses.text: When King Hezekiah heard, he tore his garments, put on sackcloth, and entered the Lord’s house.
verses.display_text: When King Hezekiah heard, he tore his garments, put on sackcloth, and entered the Lord’s house.

verses.text: He sent Eliakim the steward, Somnas the scribe, and the elders of the priests, clothed in sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, son of Amos.
verses.display_text: He sent Eliakim the steward, Somnas the scribe, and the elders of the priests, clothed in sackcloth, to Isaiah the prophet, son of Amos.

verses.text: They said to him, ‘Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of affliction, rebuke, and provocation. Children have reached the birth pains, but the woman giving birth has no strength.
verses.display_text: They said to him, ‘Thus says Hezekiah: This day is a day of affliction, rebuke, and provocation. Children have reached the birth pains, but the woman giving birth has no strength.

verses.text: Perhaps the Lord your God will hear all Rhapsakes’s words, whom his master the king of the Assyrians sent to reproach the living God and to blaspheme with words which the Lord your God has heard. Take up a prayer for the remnant that remains.’
verses.display_text: Perhaps the Lord your God will hear all Rhapsakes’s words, whom his master the king of the Assyrians sent to reproach the living God and to blaspheme with words which the Lord your God has heard. Take up a prayer for the remnant that remains.’

verses.text: King Hezekiah’s servants came to Isaiah.
verses.display_text: King Hezekiah’s servants came to Isaiah.

verses.text: Isaiah said to them, ‘Tell your master: Thus says the Lord: Do not fear the words you have heard, with which the king of the Assyrians’ young servants blasphemed.
verses.display_text: Isaiah said to them, ‘Tell your master: Thus says the Lord: Do not fear the words you have heard, with which the king of the Assyrians’ young servants blasphemed.

verses.text: Behold, I am putting a spirit within him. He shall hear a report and return to his land, and I shall bring him down by the sword in his land.’
verses.display_text: Behold, I am putting a spirit within him. He shall hear a report and return to his land, and I shall bring him down by the sword in his land.’

verses.text: Rhapsakes returned and found the king of the Assyrians fighting against Lomna, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.
verses.display_text: Rhapsakes returned and found the king of the Assyrians fighting against Lomna, for he had heard that he had departed from Lachish.

verses.text: He heard concerning Tharaka king of the Ethiopians, ‘Behold, he has come out to fight you.’ He returned and sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,
verses.display_text: He heard concerning Tharaka king of the Ethiopians, ‘Behold, he has come out to fight you.’ He returned and sent messengers to Hezekiah, saying,

verses.text: ‘Do not let your God, in whom you trust, lift you up by saying, “Jerusalem will certainly not be handed into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.”
verses.display_text: ‘Do not let your God, in whom you trust, lift you up by saying, “Jerusalem will certainly not be handed into the hands of the king of the Assyrians.”

verses.text: Behold, you have heard everything the kings of the Assyrians did to all the lands, devoting them to destruction. And will you be rescued?
verses.display_text: Behold, you have heard everything the kings of the Assyrians did to all the lands, devoting them to destruction. And will you be rescued?

verses.text: Did the gods of the nations my fathers destroyed rescue them—Gozan, Charran, Raphes, and the sons of Edem in Thaesthen?
verses.display_text: Did the gods of the nations my fathers destroyed rescue them—Gozan, Charran, Raphes, and the sons of Edem in Thaesthen?

verses.text: Where are the king of Aimath and the king of Arphad? And where are Seppharouain, Ana, and Ava?’
verses.display_text: Where are the king of Aimath and the king of Arphad? And where are Seppharouain, Ana, and Ava?’

verses.text: Hezekiah took the letters from the messengers’ hand and read them. He went up to the Lord’s house, and Hezekiah unfolded them before the Lord.
verses.display_text: Hezekiah took the letters from the messengers’ hand and read them. He went up to the Lord’s house, and Hezekiah unfolded them before the Lord.

verses.text: He said, ‘Lord, Israel’s God, seated upon the cherubim, Thou alone art God among all the kingdoms of the earth. Thou madest heaven and earth.
verses.display_text: He said, ‘Lord, Israel’s God, seated upon the cherubim, Thou alone art God among all the kingdoms of the earth. Thou madest heaven and earth.

verses.text: Incline Thine ear, Lord, and hear. Open Thine eyes, Lord, and see. Hear Sennacherib’s words, which he sent to reproach the living God.
verses.display_text: Incline Thine ear, Lord, and hear. Open Thine eyes, Lord, and see. Hear Sennacherib’s words, which he sent to reproach the living God.

verses.text: For truly, Lord, the kings of the Assyrians have devastated the nations
verses.display_text: For truly, Lord, the kings of the Assyrians have devastated the nations

verses.text: and put their gods into the fire, for they are not gods but the work of human hands, wood and stones; so they destroyed them.
verses.display_text: and put their gods into the fire, for they are not gods but the work of human hands, wood and stones; so they destroyed them.

verses.text: Now, Lord our God, save us from his hand, and all the kingdoms of the earth will know that Thou art the Lord, God alone.’
verses.display_text: Now, Lord our God, save us from his hand, and all the kingdoms of the earth will know that Thou art the Lord, God alone.’

verses.text: Isaiah son of Amos sent to Hezekiah: ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, Israel’s God: What you did pray to Me concerning Sennacherib king of the Assyrians, I have heard.
verses.display_text: Isaiah son of Amos sent to Hezekiah: ‘Thus says the Lord, the God of hosts, Israel’s God: What you did pray to Me concerning Sennacherib king of the Assyrians, I have heard.

verses.text: This is the word the Lord has spoken concerning him: Virgin daughter Zion despises you and sneers at you; daughter Jerusalem shakes her head at you.
verses.display_text: This is the word the Lord has spoken concerning him: Virgin daughter Zion despises you and sneers at you; daughter Jerusalem shakes her head at you.

verses.text: Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice? You have lifted your eyes on high against Israel’s Holy One!
verses.display_text: Whom have you reproached and blasphemed? Against whom have you raised your voice? You have lifted your eyes on high against Israel’s Holy One!

verses.text: Through your messengers you did reproach the Lord and did say, “With the multitude of my chariots I shall climb the mountain heights, Lebanon’s flanks. I cut down its cedar’s height, its choice cypresses, and came to the melon of its farthest part, the woodland of its Carmel.
verses.display_text: Through your messengers you did reproach the Lord and did say, “With the multitude of my chariots I shall climb the mountain heights, Lebanon’s flanks. I cut down its cedar’s height, its choice cypresses, and came to the melon of its farthest part, the woodland of its Carmel.

verses.text: I cooled and drank foreign waters, and with my foot’s tread I dried up all rivers of enclosure.”
verses.display_text: I cooled and drank foreign waters, and with my foot’s tread I dried up all rivers of enclosure.”

verses.text: I formed it; now I brought it. It became a carrying away into exiles of fighting men—fortified cities.
verses.display_text: I formed it; now I brought it. It became a carrying away into exiles of fighting men—fortified cities.

verses.text: Their inhabitants grew weak in hand, cowered, and were ashamed. They became field grass or green herbage, rooftop grass, and a trampling before one standing.
verses.display_text: Their inhabitants grew weak in hand, cowered, and were ashamed. They became field grass or green herbage, rooftop grass, and a trampling before one standing.

verses.text: I know your sitting, your going out, your coming in, and your anger against Me.
verses.display_text: I know your sitting, your going out, your coming in, and your anger against Me.

verses.text: Because you were angry with Me and your arrogance rose to My ears, I shall put My hooks in your nostrils and a bridle in your lips, and turn you back by the road on which you came.
verses.display_text: Because you were angry with Me and your arrogance rose to My ears, I shall put My hooks in your nostrils and a bridle in your lips, and turn you back by the road on which you came.

verses.text: This shall be the sign for you: You shall eat this year what grows by itself, and in the second year what sprouts. In the third, sowing, harvest, and planting vineyards; you shall eat their fruit.
verses.display_text: This shall be the sign for you: You shall eat this year what grows by itself, and in the second year what sprouts. In the third, sowing, harvest, and planting vineyards; you shall eat their fruit.

verses.text: The rescued remnant of Judah’s house shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.
verses.display_text: The rescued remnant of Judah’s house shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.

verses.text: For a remnant shall come out from Jerusalem, and one escaping from Mount Zion. The zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this.
verses.display_text: For a remnant shall come out from Jerusalem, and one escaping from Mount Zion. The zeal of the Lord of hosts shall do this.

verses.text: Not so! Thus says the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians: He shall not enter this city or shoot an arrow there; no shield shall come before it, and he shall certainly not pour up a siege ramp against it.
verses.display_text: Not so! Thus says the Lord concerning the king of the Assyrians: He shall not enter this city or shoot an arrow there; no shield shall come before it, and he shall certainly not pour up a siege ramp against it.

verses.text: By the road on which he came he shall return; he shall not enter this city, says the Lord.
verses.display_text: By the road on which he came he shall return; he shall not enter this city, says the Lord.

verses.text: I shall shield this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.’
verses.display_text: I shall shield this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.’

verses.text: By night the Lord’s angel went out and struck one hundred eighty-five thousand in the Assyrians’ camp. When they rose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead bodies.
verses.display_text: By night the Lord’s angel went out and struck one hundred eighty-five thousand in the Assyrians’ camp. When they rose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead bodies.

verses.text: Sennacherib king of the Assyrians departed, went away, returned, and lived in Nineveh.
verses.display_text: Sennacherib king of the Assyrians departed, went away, returned, and lived in Nineveh.

verses.text: As he was bowing down in the house of Neserach his god, his sons Adramelech and Sarasar struck him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. His son Asordan became king in his place.
verses.display_text: As he was bowing down in the house of Neserach his god, his sons Adramelech and Sarasar struck him with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. His son Asordan became king in his place.

verses.text: In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death. Isaiah son of Amos the prophet came to him and said, ‘Thus says the Lord: Give instructions for your house, for you are dying and shall not live.’
verses.display_text: In those days Hezekiah became sick to the point of death. Isaiah son of Amos the prophet came to him and said, ‘Thus says the Lord: Give instructions for your house, for you are dying and shall not live.’

verses.text: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord,
verses.display_text: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and prayed to the Lord,

verses.text: ‘I pray Thee, Lord, remember how I walked before Thee in truth and with a full heart, and did what was good in Thine eyes.’ Hezekiah wept bitterly.
verses.display_text: ‘I pray Thee, Lord, remember how I walked before Thee in truth and with a full heart, and did what was good in Thine eyes.’ Hezekiah wept bitterly.

verses.text: Isaiah was in the middle courtyard when the Lord’s word came to him:
verses.display_text: Isaiah was in the middle courtyard when the Lord’s word came to him:

verses.text: ‘Return and tell Hezekiah, leader of My people: Thus says the Lord, the God of your father David: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Behold, I shall heal you; on the third day you shall go up to the Lord’s house,
verses.display_text: ‘Return and tell Hezekiah, leader of My people: Thus says the Lord, the God of your father David: I have heard your prayer and seen your tears. Behold, I shall heal you; on the third day you shall go up to the Lord’s house,

verses.text: and I shall add fifteen years to your days. I shall save you and this city from the hand of the king of the Assyrians, and shield this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.’
verses.display_text: and I shall add fifteen years to your days. I shall save you and this city from the hand of the king of the Assyrians, and shield this city for My own sake and for the sake of David My servant.’

verses.text: He said, ‘Let them take a cake of figs and place it on the ulcer, and he will recover.’
verses.display_text: He said, ‘Let them take a cake of figs and place it on the ulcer, and he will recover.’

verses.text: Hezekiah said to Isaiah, ‘What is the sign that the Lord will heal me and I shall go up to the Lord’s house on the third day?’
verses.display_text: Hezekiah said to Isaiah, ‘What is the sign that the Lord will heal me and I shall go up to the Lord’s house on the third day?’

verses.text: Isaiah said, ‘This is the sign from the Lord that the Lord will do the word He has spoken: The shadow will advance ten steps, if it returns ten steps.’
verses.display_text: Isaiah said, ‘This is the sign from the Lord that the Lord will do the word He has spoken: The shadow will advance ten steps, if it returns ten steps.’

verses.text: Hezekiah said, ‘It is easy for the shadow to incline ten steps. No, let the shadow return ten steps backward.’
verses.display_text: Hezekiah said, ‘It is easy for the shadow to incline ten steps. No, let the shadow return ten steps backward.’

verses.text: Isaiah the prophet cried to the Lord, and the shadow returned backward ten steps on the stairway.
verses.display_text: Isaiah the prophet cried to the Lord, and the shadow returned backward ten steps on the stairway.

verses.text: At that time Marodachbaladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and manaa to Hezekiah, because he heard that Hezekiah was sick.
verses.display_text: At that time Marodachbaladan son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and manaa to Hezekiah, because he heard that Hezekiah was sick.

verses.text: Hezekiah rejoiced over them and showed them the whole house of the nechotha: the silver, gold, spices, fine oil, the house of equipment, and everything found in his treasuries. There was nothing in his house or all his authority that Hezekiah did not show them.
verses.display_text: Hezekiah rejoiced over them and showed them the whole house of the nechotha: the silver, gold, spices, fine oil, the house of equipment, and everything found in his treasuries. There was nothing in his house or all his authority that Hezekiah did not show them.

verses.text: Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said, ‘What did these men say, and from where have they come to you?’ Hezekiah said, ‘They have come to me from a distant land, from Babylon.’
verses.display_text: Isaiah the prophet came to King Hezekiah and said, ‘What did these men say, and from where have they come to you?’ Hezekiah said, ‘They have come to me from a distant land, from Babylon.’

verses.text: He said, ‘What have they seen in your house?’ He said, ‘They saw everything in my house. There was nothing in my house that I did not show them, and also the things in my treasuries.’
verses.display_text: He said, ‘What have they seen in your house?’ He said, ‘They saw everything in my house. There was nothing in my house that I did not show them, and also the things in my treasuries.’

verses.text: Isaiah said to Hezekiah, ‘Hear the Lord’s word:
verses.display_text: Isaiah said to Hezekiah, ‘Hear the Lord’s word:

verses.text: Behold, days are coming when everything in your house, and what your fathers stored up to this day, shall be taken to Babylon. No word which the Lord spoke shall be left over.
verses.display_text: Behold, days are coming when everything in your house, and what your fathers stored up to this day, shall be taken to Babylon. No word which the Lord spoke shall be left over.

verses.text: He shall take your sons who come forth from you, whom you beget, and they shall be eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon.’
verses.display_text: He shall take your sons who come forth from you, whom you beget, and they shall be eunuchs in the house of the king of Babylon.’

verses.text: Hezekiah said to Isaiah, ‘The word of the Lord which He spoke is good. Let there be peace in my days.’
verses.display_text: Hezekiah said to Isaiah, ‘The word of the Lord which He spoke is good. Let there be peace in my days.’

verses.text: The rest of Hezekiah’s deeds, all his might, and what he made—the fountain and aqueduct—and how he brought water into the city—are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.display_text: The rest of Hezekiah’s deeds, all his might, and what he made—the fountain and aqueduct—and how he brought water into the city—are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

verses.text: Hezekiah lay down with his fathers and was buried in David’s city. His son Manasseh became king in his place.
verses.display_text: Hezekiah lay down with his fathers and was buried in David’s city. His son Manasseh became king in his place.

verses.text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Opsiba.
verses.display_text: Manasseh was twelve years old when he became king, and he reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Opsiba.

verses.text: He did evil in the Lord’s eyes, according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord removed before the Israelites.
verses.display_text: He did evil in the Lord’s eyes, according to the abominations of the nations whom the Lord removed before the Israelites.

verses.text: He rebuilt the high places his father Hezekiah had pulled down, erected an altar for Baal, and made groves as Ahab king of Israel had done. He bowed down to all heaven’s host and served them.
verses.display_text: He rebuilt the high places his father Hezekiah had pulled down, erected an altar for Baal, and made groves as Ahab king of Israel had done. He bowed down to all heaven’s host and served them.

verses.text: He built an altar in the Lord’s house, as He had said, ‘In Jerusalem I shall place My name.’
verses.display_text: He built an altar in the Lord’s house, as He had said, ‘In Jerusalem I shall place My name.’

verses.text: He built an altar for all heaven’s host in the two courts of the Lord’s house.
verses.display_text: He built an altar for all heaven’s host in the two courts of the Lord’s house.

verses.text: He led his sons through fire, practiced divination from sounds, read omens, and appointed a charmer and knowing ones. He did much evil in the Lord’s eyes, provoking Him.
verses.display_text: He led his sons through fire, practiced divination from sounds, read omens, and appointed a charmer and knowing ones. He did much evil in the Lord’s eyes, provoking Him.

verses.text: He placed the carved image of the grove in the house of which the Lord said to David and his son Solomon, ‘In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all Israel’s tribes, I shall place My name there for ever.
verses.display_text: He placed the carved image of the grove in the house of which the Lord said to David and his son Solomon, ‘In this house and in Jerusalem, which I chose from all Israel’s tribes, I shall place My name there for ever.

verses.text: I shall no longer shake Israel’s foot from the land I gave their fathers, for those who keep everything I commanded according to the whole commandment My servant Moses commanded them.’
verses.display_text: I shall no longer shake Israel’s foot from the land I gave their fathers, for those who keep everything I commanded according to the whole commandment My servant Moses commanded them.’

verses.text: But they did not listen. Manasseh led them astray to do evil in the Lord’s eyes beyond the nations whom the Lord obliterated before the Israelites.
verses.display_text: But they did not listen. Manasseh led them astray to do evil in the Lord’s eyes beyond the nations whom the Lord obliterated before the Israelites.

verses.text: The Lord spoke through His servants the prophets:
verses.display_text: The Lord spoke through His servants the prophets:

verses.text: ‘Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these evil abominations, worse than everything the Amorite before him did, and has also caused Judah to sin through their idols,
verses.display_text: ‘Because Manasseh king of Judah has done these evil abominations, worse than everything the Amorite before him did, and has also caused Judah to sin through their idols,

verses.text: not so! Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Behold, I am bringing disasters upon Jerusalem and Judah, so that both ears of everyone hearing shall ring.
verses.display_text: not so! Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Behold, I am bringing disasters upon Jerusalem and Judah, so that both ears of everyone hearing shall ring.

verses.text: I shall stretch over Jerusalem Samaria’s measure and the weight of Ahab’s house. I shall wipe Jerusalem as an alabaster jar is wiped, wiped and overturned on its face.
verses.display_text: I shall stretch over Jerusalem Samaria’s measure and the weight of Ahab’s house. I shall wipe Jerusalem as an alabaster jar is wiped, wiped and overturned on its face.

verses.text: I shall reject the remnant of My inheritance and hand them into their enemies’ hands. They shall become plunder and booty for all their enemies,
verses.display_text: I shall reject the remnant of My inheritance and hand them into their enemies’ hands. They shall become plunder and booty for all their enemies,

verses.text: because they did evil in My eyes and provoked Me from the day I brought their fathers out of Egypt until this day.’
verses.display_text: because they did evil in My eyes and provoked Me from the day I brought their fathers out of Egypt until this day.’

verses.text: Manasseh also poured out very much innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem from end to end, besides his sins by which he caused Judah to do evil in the Lord’s eyes.
verses.display_text: Manasseh also poured out very much innocent blood, until he filled Jerusalem from end to end, besides his sins by which he caused Judah to do evil in the Lord’s eyes.

verses.text: The rest of Manasseh’s deeds, all that he did, and the sin he committed—are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.display_text: The rest of Manasseh’s deeds, all that he did, and the sin he committed—are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

verses.text: Manasseh lay down with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his house, in Oza’s garden. His son Amon became king in his place.
verses.display_text: Manasseh lay down with his fathers and was buried in the garden of his house, in Oza’s garden. His son Amon became king in his place.

verses.text: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Mesollam daughter of Arous, from Jeteba.
verses.display_text: Amon was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned two years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Mesollam daughter of Arous, from Jeteba.

verses.text: He did evil in the Lord’s eyes, as his father Manasseh had done.
verses.display_text: He did evil in the Lord’s eyes, as his father Manasseh had done.

verses.text: He walked in every way his father had walked, served the idols his father had served, and bowed down to them.
verses.display_text: He walked in every way his father had walked, served the idols his father had served, and bowed down to them.

verses.text: He abandoned the Lord, the God of his fathers, and did not walk in the Lord’s way.
verses.display_text: He abandoned the Lord, the God of his fathers, and did not walk in the Lord’s way.

verses.text: Amon’s servants conspired against him and put the king to death in his house.
verses.display_text: Amon’s servants conspired against him and put the king to death in his house.

verses.text: All the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amon. The people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.
verses.display_text: All the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amon. The people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.

verses.text: The rest of Amon’s deeds, what he did—behold, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
verses.display_text: The rest of Amon’s deeds, what he did—behold, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

verses.text: They buried him in his tomb in Oza’s garden. His son Josiah became king in his place.
verses.display_text: They buried him in his tomb in Oza’s garden. His son Josiah became king in his place.

verses.text: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jedida daughter of Edeia, from Basouroth.
verses.display_text: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Jedida daughter of Edeia, from Basouroth.

verses.text: He did what was right in the Lord’s eyes and walked in every way of his father David, turning aside neither right nor left.
verses.display_text: He did what was right in the Lord’s eyes and walked in every way of his father David, turning aside neither right nor left.

verses.text: In King Josiah’s eighteenth year, in the eighth month, the king sent Sapphan son of Eselias son of Mesollam, the scribe of the Lord’s house, saying,
verses.display_text: In King Josiah’s eighteenth year, in the eighth month, the king sent Sapphan son of Eselias son of Mesollam, the scribe of the Lord’s house, saying,

verses.text: ‘Go up to Chelkias the high priest and seal the silver brought into the Lord’s house, which those guarding the doorpost collected from the people.
verses.display_text: ‘Go up to Chelkias the high priest and seal the silver brought into the Lord’s house, which those guarding the doorpost collected from the people.

verses.text: Let them give it into the hand of the workers appointed in the Lord’s house.’ He gave it to the workers in the Lord’s house to strengthen the house’s bedek:
verses.display_text: Let them give it into the hand of the workers appointed in the Lord’s house.’ He gave it to the workers in the Lord’s house to strengthen the house’s bedek:

verses.text: to the carpenters, builders, and wall builders, and to acquire timber and quarried stones to strengthen the house’s bedek.
verses.display_text: to the carpenters, builders, and wall builders, and to acquire timber and quarried stones to strengthen the house’s bedek.

verses.text: But they did not demand an account from them for the silver given to them, for they act faithfully.
verses.display_text: But they did not demand an account from them for the silver given to them, for they act faithfully.

verses.text: Chelkias the high priest said to Sapphan the scribe, ‘I found a book of the law in the Lord’s house.’ Chelkias gave the book to Sapphan, and he read it.
verses.display_text: Chelkias the high priest said to Sapphan the scribe, ‘I found a book of the law in the Lord’s house.’ Chelkias gave the book to Sapphan, and he read it.

verses.text: He brought it to King Josiah, reported to the king, and said, ‘Your servants have melted down the silver found in the Lord’s house and given it into the hand of the workers appointed in the Lord’s house.’
verses.display_text: He brought it to King Josiah, reported to the king, and said, ‘Your servants have melted down the silver found in the Lord’s house and given it into the hand of the workers appointed in the Lord’s house.’

verses.text: Sapphan the scribe told the king, ‘Chelkias the priest gave me a book.’ Sapphan read it before the king.
verses.display_text: Sapphan the scribe told the king, ‘Chelkias the priest gave me a book.’ Sapphan read it before the king.

verses.text: When the king heard the words of the book of the law, he tore his garments.
verses.display_text: When the king heard the words of the book of the law, he tore his garments.

verses.text: The king commanded Chelkias the priest, Achikam son of Sapphan, Achobor son of Michaias, Sapphan the scribe, and Asaia the king’s servant:
verses.display_text: The king commanded Chelkias the priest, Achikam son of Sapphan, Achobor son of Michaias, Sapphan the scribe, and Asaia the king’s servant:

verses.text: ‘Come, seek the Lord for me, for all the people, and for all Judah concerning the words of this book that has been found. For great is the Lord’s anger which burns among us, because our fathers did not listen to this book’s words, to do everything written against us.’
verses.display_text: ‘Come, seek the Lord for me, for all the people, and for all Judah concerning the words of this book that has been found. For great is the Lord’s anger which burns among us, because our fathers did not listen to this book’s words, to do everything written against us.’

verses.text: Chelkias the priest, Achikam, Achobor, Sapphan, and Asaias went to Olda the prophetess, wife of Sellem son of Thekoue son of Araas, keeper of the garments. She lived in Jerusalem in the masena. They spoke to her.
verses.display_text: Chelkias the priest, Achikam, Achobor, Sapphan, and Asaias went to Olda the prophetess, wife of Sellem son of Thekoue son of Araas, keeper of the garments. She lived in Jerusalem in the masena. They spoke to her.

verses.text: She said to them, ‘Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Tell the man who sent you to me:
verses.display_text: She said to them, ‘Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: Tell the man who sent you to me:

verses.text: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing disasters on this place and its inhabitants, all the words of the book which the king of Judah has read,
verses.display_text: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am bringing disasters on this place and its inhabitants, all the words of the book which the king of Judah has read,

verses.text: because they abandoned Me and burned incense to other gods, provoking Me with the works of their hands. My wrath shall burn against this place and shall not be quenched.
verses.display_text: because they abandoned Me and burned incense to other gods, provoking Me with the works of their hands. My wrath shall burn against this place and shall not be quenched.

verses.text: But to the king of Judah who sent you to seek the Lord, say this: Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: The words you have heard—
verses.display_text: But to the king of Judah who sent you to seek the Lord, say this: Thus says the Lord, Israel’s God: The words you have heard—

verses.text: because your heart was softened and you did feel shame before the Lord when you heard what I spoke against this place and its inhabitants, that they should become an obliteration and a curse, and because you did rend your garments and did weep before Me, I also have heard, says the Lord.
verses.display_text: because your heart was softened and you did feel shame before the Lord when you heard what I spoke against this place and its inhabitants, that they should become an obliteration and a curse, and because you did rend your garments and did weep before Me, I also have heard, says the Lord.

verses.text: Not so! Behold, I am adding you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered into your grave in peace. None of all the disasters I am bringing upon this place shall appear before your eyes.’ They reported the word to the king.
verses.display_text: Not so! Behold, I am adding you to your fathers, and you shall be gathered into your grave in peace. None of all the disasters I am bringing upon this place shall appear before your eyes.’ They reported the word to the king.

verses.text: The king sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.
verses.display_text: The king sent and gathered to himself all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

verses.text: The king went up to the Lord’s house, with every man of Judah and all who inhabited Jerusalem, the priests, the prophets, and all the people, from small to great. He read in their hearing all the words of the covenant book found in the Lord’s house.
verses.display_text: The king went up to the Lord’s house, with every man of Judah and all who inhabited Jerusalem, the priests, the prophets, and all the people, from small to great. He read in their hearing all the words of the covenant book found in the Lord’s house.

verses.text: The king stood beside the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord: to follow the Lord and keep His commandments, testimonies, and ordinances with the whole heart and whole soul, upholding the words of this covenant, the things written in this book. All the people stood in the covenant.
verses.display_text: The king stood beside the pillar and made a covenant before the Lord: to follow the Lord and keep His commandments, testimonies, and ordinances with the whole heart and whole soul, upholding the words of this covenant, the things written in this book. All the people stood in the covenant.

verses.text: The king commanded Chelkias the high priest, the priests of the second rank, and the doorpost guards to bring out of the Lord’s sanctuary all the vessels made for Baal, for the grove, and for all heaven’s host. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the sademoth of Kidron and took their dust to Bethel.
verses.display_text: The king commanded Chelkias the high priest, the priests of the second rank, and the doorpost guards to bring out of the Lord’s sanctuary all the vessels made for Baal, for the grove, and for all heaven’s host. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the sademoth of Kidron and took their dust to Bethel.

verses.text: He put an end to the chomarim whom Judah’s kings had appointed, who burned incense at the high places and in Judah’s cities and the places around Jerusalem, and to those burning incense to Baal, the sun, the moon, the mazouroth, and all heaven’s host.

Turning, he lifted his eyes toward the tomb of the man of God who had spoken these words.

verses.text: For this Passover had not occurred since the days of the judges who judged Israel, throughout all the days of Israel’s kings and Judah’s kings.

verses.text: King Josiah also removed the charmers, the knowing ones, the theraphin, the idols, and all the offensive things present in Judah’s land and Jerusalem, to uphold the law’s words written in the book Chelkias the priest found in the Lord’s house.

verses.text: Before him there was no king like him who returned to the Lord with his whole heart, his whole soul, and all his strength, according to all Moses’ law; and after him none like him arose.

verses.display_text: The Lord said, ‘I shall also remove Judah from My presence, as I removed Israel. I shall reject this city which I chose, Jerusalem, and the house of which I said, “My name shall be there.”’

verses.display_text: Joachas was twenty-three years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Amital daughter of Jeremiah, from Lemna.

verses.text: He sent against him the lightly equipped raiders of the Chaldeans, Syria, Moab, and the Ammonites. He sent them out in Judah’s land to prevail, according to the Lord’s word which He spoke through His servants the prophets.

verses.display_text: Joakim lay down with his fathers, and his son Joakim became king in his place.
